incoming.name: Caroline Island
incoming.excerpt: Caroline Island and its neighbour, Flint Island, also host some of the world's largest populations of the coconut crab. (Birgus latro).

incoming.name: Christmas Island
incoming.excerpt: Robber crabs, known elsewhere as coconut crabs, also exist in large numbers on the island.

outgoing.name: Bay of Bengal
outgoing.excerpt: They are also known on several of the Andaman and Nicobar Islands in the Bay of Bengal.

outgoing.name: Caroline Island
outgoing.excerpt: However, according to some reports the populations are quite large, with one of the largest populations being on Caroline Island.

outgoing.name: Christmas Island
outgoing.excerpt: Christmas Island in the Indian Ocean has the largest and best-preserved population in the world.

outgoing.name: Coconut
outgoing.excerpt: It is a derived hermit crab which is known for its ability to crack coconuts with its strong pincers in order to eat the contents.

outgoing.name: Cook Islands
outgoing.excerpt: Large populations also exist on the Cook Islands ( Pacific Islands), especially Pukapuka, Suwarrow, Mangaia, Takutea, Mauke, Atiu and smaller islands of Palmerston.

outgoing.name: Extinction
outgoing.excerpt: This is due to the coconut crabs being eaten to extinction by people.

outgoing.name: Guam
outgoing.excerpt: The coconut crab also has different local names as for example ayuyu in Guam, or unga or kaveu.

outgoing.name: Japan
outgoing.excerpt: It may also be possible that this poison is considered an aphrodisiac, similar to the highly poisonous pufferfish eaten in Japan.

outgoing.name: Pig
outgoing.excerpt: The juvenile coconut crab is vulnerable to introduced carnivores such as rats, pigs, or ants such as the yellow crazy ant.

outgoing.name: Sand
outgoing.excerpt: They dig their own burrows in sand or loose soil.

outgoing.name: Tide
outgoing.excerpt: At the time of hatching, usually October or November, the female coconut crab releases the eggs into the ocean at high tide.

outgoing.name: Tokyo
outgoing.excerpt: The coconut crab, especially if it is not yet fully grown, is also sold as a pet, for example in Tokyo.
